263: Voted best campground in West Virginia by campingprepper.com.  The primitive sites take only small rigs. --Claude
970: Resort near Berlin and Ocean City, minutes from the beach and boardwalk, with a boat ramp, a pool and a restaurant. --Claude
1165: At Fallentimber (Cambria County), about 2 miles from Glendale Lake and Prince Gallitzin State Park, with a creek on the property. --Claude
1167: 75-acre resort near Rockwood (Somerset County) with wide, level sites and a 5-acre fishing lake; the lakeside units are covered-wagon rentals, not RV sites. --Claude
1182: Family campground on the Upper Delaware River at Equinunk (Wayne County), just above Kellam's Bridge.  Only ten sites suit RVs, for trailers up to 40 ft on narrow, uneven roads; the full-hookup sites are seasonal.  Riverfront sites need at least 6 adults and creekside sites 4, and some RV sites carry a 3-adult minimum. --Claude
1183: Formerly Sheshequin Campground, at Trout Run (Lycoming County), with two cabins, a bathhouse and a creek used for fishing and tubing; the sites take any size RV.  Open April through October. --Claude
1184: 57-acre family campground near Tunkhannock (Wyoming County) with a 12-acre fishing lake and a swimming pond; the overnight RV sites sit by one or the other.  Also listed on Hipcamp. --Claude
1218: 28-acre campground near Elkins (Randolph County) in the National Radio Quiet Zone, bordering Chenoweth Creek; 13 of the RV sites have full hookups.  Self check-in, no office. --Claude
1224: Small, wooded RV park ten minutes from the west side of Clarksburg (Harrison County), pitched mainly at traveling workers on long stays but selling nightly sites year-round; all sites are back-ins.  Booked by phone: Campspot lists the park but had no sites to book on 2026-10-13, and no nightly rate is posted. --Claude
1226: Raleigh County park near Beckley on 272-acre Lake Stephens, with a marina, a beach, cabins and a separate tent campground.  The RV loop sits back from the lake; its sites are tight and treeless. --Claude
1243: Perry Township (Lake County) park on a Lake Erie bluff; the sites along the bluff look out over the lake.  Open roughly May to November; many sites are seasonal, but nightly sites are sold. --Claude
1250: Village of Plain City campground: 38 grass sites and 18 gravel pads (70 by 15 feet).  Open April through October. --Claude
1262: Large campground beside an RV dealership, with a creek and a fishing pond; 54 of its sites are sold by the night.  Some sites need a 50-75 ft water hose, and the creekside ones a 30-40 ft extension cord too. --Claude
1264: Sites ring an 8-acre lake used for swimming and fishing, some on the water and some looking at it, with a boat ramp.  Open May through October. --Claude
1325: Vigo County park on Burns Lake; some sites look straight out over the lake. --Claude
1327: Vigo County park on Fowler Lake south of Terre Haute.  Some electric sites sit right on the lake but are short, so check the length for a 23-ft rig. --Claude
1331: Tipton County fairgrounds, with a bathhouse. --Claude
1332: Delaware County fairgrounds in Muncie, within walking distance of downtown; few sites are truly level for a big rig. --Claude
1337: Town of Vevay campground in Ogle Park on the Ohio River, with gravel sites (12 with full hookups), a boat launch and a dog park. --Claude
1340: Vigo County park near Terre Haute, with sites in a maple grove beside a 13-acre lake and a pond. --Claude
1342: Sullivan County Park & Lake Board park on 461-acre Sullivan Lake; the nightly RV sites are back-ins on gravel pads.  Open roughly March to October. --Claude
1356: Veteran-owned campground on reclaimed mine land in the Bluegrass Fish and Wildlife Area, with ponds nearby. --Claude
1359: Family-owned Christian campground near Richmond; the Middle Fork of the Whitewater River runs through the property. --Claude
